lines.t: Spirit of YahuShua, come and search the inner‑man,
Walk back through the memory rooms I never let You in.
Where fathers’ words and mothers’ fears
Became the law inside my ears,
Where playground names and glowing screens
Drew crooked lines on who I’d be.
They told me I was “too much,” then they told me I was “not enough,”
So I learned to hide my heart and wear a tougher kind of love.
Every channel, every song,
Taught me how to play along,
To chase a face that wasn’t mine,
And leave my little child behind.
So I stand here in Your presence, with the question on my tongue:
When did I stop loving myself, when did I turn and run?
When did you stop loving yourself?
Was it in a bedroom, whisper‑dark, where shame first learned your name?
When did you lock up your heart on the shelf,
Believing every lie that said you’d never be the same?
Spirit of YahuShua, shine Your light where my secrets dwell,
Show me where the wound began, when I stopped loving myself.
Spirit, take me deeper still, beneath the fear and guarded will,
To every place I chose the crowd
Over the gentle voice that called.
To every look I saw in church
That said I had to earn my worth,
To every rule of men that screamed
I’d fall too far to be redeemed.
I breathed in messages of fear,
Where judgment thundered, love was veiled,
Where threats were louder than Your grace,
And You seemed distant from my shame.
So I turned their voices on my soul,
Made their harshness my own goal,
Till a darker question took its throne
And whispered like it was my own:
If I can’t love the one You made, maybe You don’t love me,
So trembling, I dare ask You now the question secretly:
When did God stop loving me?
Was it when my hands were dirty, when my secrets came to light?
Did Your gaze grow cold and distant
When I wandered in the night?
But in the silence of my fear, a softer truth surrounds me:
You have always seen my heart, and You have never turned away,
Your love was holding every scar, even when I ran astray.
Love says, “You are precious to Me, closer than your breath,
Desired from the very start, not an accident.
I have watched you, bruised and fragile,
Kept your tears inside My hands,
Waited for the day you’d know
You were never less than planned.”
Love says, “I gave up all for you,
Chose the cross and bore your pain,
Let My own body be broken
So your heart could live again.
I have carried you in secret,
Through the nights you thought were lost,
Nothing you have done or suffered
Could outweigh that crimson cost.”
And the Scriptures echo mercy,
From the garden to the tree:
Love that moves toward broken sinners,
Love that will not cease to be.
If You love me so much, why don’t I love myself?
Why do I speak to Your creation like it’s something else?
Why do I starve the soul You feed,
Withhold the grace that I receive,
Refuse the face Your hands have drawn,
And curse the child You’ve waited on?
I feel You whisper to my heart,
“Let go of this accusing voice,
Lay down every borrowed verdict,
I have made another choice.
You are Mine and I am for you,
Not ashamed to call you close,
Come and rest upon My kindness,
Let My joy define your soul.”
So here I bring my mirrored hate,
Lay down my self‑despising weight,
I break agreement with the lie
That You regretted giving life.
Spirit of YahuShua, testify within my chest,
That loving what You lovingly have made is holy rest.
If He loves me with an endless flame,
Then I can bless the work of His hands and call it by His name.
If He sings over me with delight,
Then I can look into my eyes and see a child of light.
I give myself permission now to love the one He’s fashioned,
To speak His words over my frame, not curses born of passion.
For the love that hung upon that tree
Whispers, “You may love you too, because you are loved by Me.”
